title: Timor-Leste
wiki_lead:
Timor-Leste, also known as East Timor, officially the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste, is a country in Southeast Asia. It comprises the eastern half of the island of Timor, the coastal exclave of Oecusse in the island's northwest, and the islands of Atauro and Jaco, for a total land area of 15,007 square kilometres (5,794 sq mi). Timor-Leste shares a land border with Indonesia to the west; Australia is the country's southern neighbour, across the Timor Sea. Dili, on the north coast of Timor, is its capital and largest city.
Timor was settled over time by various Papuan and Austronesian peoples, which created a diverse mix of cultures and languages linked to Southeast Asia and Melanesia. East Timor came under Portuguese influence in the sixteenth century, remaining a Portuguese colony until 1975. Internal conflict preceded a unilateral declaration of independence and an Indonesian invasion and annexation. The subsequent Indonesian occupation was characterised by extreme abuses of human rights, including torture and massacres, a series of events named the East Timor genocide. Resistance continued throughout Indonesian rule and in 1999, a United Nations–sponsored act of self-determination led Indonesia to relinquish control of the territory. On 20 May 2002, Timor-Leste became the first new sovereign state of the 21st century. That same year, relations with Indonesia were established and normalised, with Indonesia also supporting Timor-Leste's accession into ASEAN.
The national government is a semi-presidential system, with the popularly elected president sharing power with a prime minister appointed by the National Parliament. Power is centralised under the national government, although many local leaders have informal influence. The country maintains a policy of international cooperation and is a member of the Community of Portuguese Language Countries and ASEAN, and is an observer of the Pacific Islands Forum. The country remains relatively poor, with an economy that relies heavily on natural resources, especially oil, and foreign aid.
The total population is over 1.44 million at the 2026 census, and is heavily skewed towards young people because of a high fertility rate. Education has led to increasing literacy over the past half-century, especially in the two official languages of Portuguese and Tetun. High ethnic and linguistic diversity is reflected by the 30 indigenous languages spoken in the country. Most of the population practices Roman Catholicism, which coexists alongside strong local traditions and beliefs, especially in rural areas.

Name
"Timor" is derived from timur, which means 'east' in Indonesian or Malay. "Leste" incidentally on the other hand also means "east" in Portuguese. Therefore, Timor-Leste simply translates to 'East East' in English. 
In Indonesian or Malay, this results in the name Timor Timur (the name of the former de facto Indonesian province; Timor Leste is used instead to refer to the country). In Tetun, it is Timór Lorosa'e (lorosa'e means "east", literally translated as 'where the sun rises').
The official names under its constitution are "Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste" in English, "República Democrática de Timor-Leste" in Portuguese, and "Repúblika Demokrátika Timór-Leste" in Tetun. The official short form of the name is "Timor-Leste", and it uses the ISO codes TLS and TL.


History


Prehistory and Classical era

Cultural remains at Jerimalai on the eastern tip of Timor-Leste have been dated to 42,000 years ago. The first known inhabitants are those who arrived during the Australo-Melanesian migration through the region, likely bringing the precursors to today's Papuan languages. A later migration of Austroasiatic-speakers is suspected, although no such languages remain. The arrival of Austronesian peoples brought new languages, and merged with existing cultures on the island. grok_lead: Timor-Leste, also known in English as East Timor, is a country in Southeast Asia. Its constitution styles the state the Democratic Republic of East Timor and defines the territory as the eastern part of the island of Timor, the enclave of Oecusse Ambeno, the island of Atauro and the islet of Jaco. The capital is Dili, and the land area is about 14,874 square kilometres. The 2022 population and housing census recorded 1,341,737 residents; World Bank data put the population at 1,418,517 in 2025. Portugal held the eastern half of Timor through the colonial period and, after the 1974 coup in Lisbon, began to withdraw. Independence was proclaimed on 28 November 1975, the date the constitution marks as the Day of the Proclamation of Independence. Indonesia invaded in December 1975 and occupied the territory until a United Nations -supervised vote in 1999, after which the UN administered the transition to independence. That independence was restored on 20 May 2002, and the General Assembly admitted the country to the United Nations the same year. The president is head of state, elected by universal suffrage for five years and eligible for one further term, and the National Parliament has between 52 and 65 members. World Bank figures put gross domestic product at about US$1.90 billion in 2025, roughly US$1,341 a person.
